Impaired tolerance permits autoimmune thyroid inflammation in selected patients. Antithyroid antibodies and variable thyroid functional states support an organ-specific autoimmune process; the precise T-cell/B-cell effectors are not resolved.

Loss of immune tolerance contributes to antibody-associated erythrocyte destruction in reported AIHA cases. Rituximab-responsive Evans syndrome supports a B-cell contribution, without identifying the initiating autoreactive clone.

Tolerance failure permits immune-mediated platelet loss in reported ITP/Evans syndrome. The receptor/Treg model is an upstream explanation; the relative platelet-clearance and production mechanisms were not established.

The tolerance-defect model provides a qualified contribution to the explicitly diagnosed autoimmune hepatitis in the Turkish series. This is separate from the unconfirmed hepatic diagnosis in the Taiwanese adult.

Defective immune tolerance offers a proposed contribution to the reported autoimmune depigmentation. The CD3G studies do not directly measure melanocyte-specific effector cells or explain why only some patients develop vitiligo.

The primary authors classify the single minimal-change nephrotic presentation among autoimmune manifestations. The tolerance model is a qualified upstream contribution; no particular podocyte-targeting antibody or T-cell mediator was established.

The 2024 authors attribute a lupus-like syndrome meeting SLICC criteria to CD3G deficiency. The tolerance model provides an indirect explanation, while organ-specific immune mechanisms remain unresolved.
Autoimmune thyroid disease can produce hypothyroidism in the reported patients; euthyroid thyroiditis and the opposite functional state also occur.

nodes.description: Biallelic CD3G variants impair the CD3gamma subunit of the TCR/CD3 complex. nodes.description: CD3gamma deficiency lowers, without invariably abolishing, surface TCR/CD3 expression in human T cells. CD3G-knockdown Jurkat cells show unstable partial receptor ensembles, ER retention and deficient zeta-dimer incorporation, but their profound receptor loss does not quantitatively reproduce patient cells. Patient-cell reconstitution supports a role for CD3gamma in surface expression; the precise assembly/export constraints depend on the cellular system. Human gamma-delta receptors can incorporate CD3delta, providing a supported explanation for partial compensation in that lineage.
